definitions.definition: The ordered eigenvalues of a reduced density matrix for a declared bipartition of a pure state; equivalently, the squared Schmidt coefficients.
definitions.scope: bipartite pure state and declared cut

definitions.definition: The time-dependent ordered spectrum t -> lambda(t), treated as the primary latent dynamical object.
A time-ordered projection of a Schmidt-spectrum path, conventionally (lambda_max(t), E[lambda(t)]) for a declared spectrum functional E.
definitions.scope: projection and metric must be declared

definitions.definition: The family of trajectories obtained by applying several declared spectrum functionals to one Schmidt-spectrum path.
A partial order on ordered probability vectors defined by cumulative-sum inequalities, used here to identify spectrum pairs on which all Schur-concave entropies agree.
The position of a metric value between its exact fixed-largest-eigenvalue minimum and maximum. It is undefined when the feasible envelope collapses.
definitions.scope: metrics with exact noncollapsed fixed-lambda_max envelopes

definitions.definition: A transition on which the tested metric classes report the same direction of change.
definitions.scope: declared metric set and numerical tolerance

definitions.definition: A transition on which the tested metric classes report different directions of change, indicating a spectral redistribution not captured by one total scalar ordering.
definitions.scope: declared metric set and numerical tolerance

definitions.definition: Coarse trajectory morphology that remains recognizable under replacement of one declared Schmidt-spectrum metric by another.
definitions.scope: empirical, declared models, metrics, cuts, and sampling

definitions.definition: A Haar/Wishart, Marchenko-Pastur, spectral-edge, bulk-correlation, or separated-spike benchmark used inside the exact feasible arena.
The number of strictly positive entries in the represented Schmidt spectrum. No support threshold is applied.
A threshold-dependent count of Schmidt-spectrum entries above a declared absolute or relative cutoff.
definitions.scope: floating-point spectral diagnostic with declared threshold

definitions.definition: The alignment variable tau=step/n. It orders and rescales sampled iterations but is not a common physical time across all dynamical families.
